summary: The root HBB primarily conveys the meaning of love, affection, and being beloved. It also encompasses the idea of producing seeds or grains, and by extension, becoming pregnant or having a full udder.

headwords.def: أَحَبُّ [ More, and most, loved, beloved, &c. You say, هٰذَا أَحَبُّ إِلَىَّ مِنْ ذَاكَ This is more an object of love, affection, liking, or approval, or is more lovely, charming, or pleasing, to me than that. And هُوَ أَحَبُّهُمْ إِلَىَّ He is the most beloved of them to me. ]

headwords.gloss: of El-Medeeneh
headwords.def: مُحَبٌّ محب : see حَبِيبٌ , in three places. المُحَبَّةُ and and and are epithets of El-Medeeneh. (K.)
مُحِبٌّ محب , and its fem.: see حَبِيبٌ , in three places.

headwords.gloss: A cause of love; affection; Such a one was gifted with

parts.t: Such a one was gifted with
the causes of the love of hearts

headwords.def: مَحَبَّةٌ محب محبه محبة : see حُبٌّ . Also A cause of love or affection: (Jel in xx. 39:) [pl. مَحَابُّ , like مَحَاشُّ pl. of مَحَشَّةٌ , &c.] You say, أُوتِىَ فُلَانٌ مَحَابَّ القُلُوبِ [ Such a one was gifted with qualities that are the causes of the love of hearts ]. (A, TA.)
مُحَبَّةٌ محب محبه محبة : see حُبَّةٌ .

headwords.gloss: i. q

headwords.gloss: The serpent
headwords.def: مَحْبُوبٌ محبوب : see حَبِيبٌ , in two places. المَحْبُوبَةُ : see مُحَبٌّ . أُمُّ مَحْبُوبٍ a surname of The serpent. (K.) [See also حُبَابٌ .]
